methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Terra Drone, a Japanese public company in the Drones & Autonomous sector founded by Toru Tokushige, presents a valuation challenge due to limited comparable data. The sector contains six private peers—including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air—but no public comparables, and insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private peers to support a robust peer-median methodology. Our comp universe analysis identified five same-sector peers overall, but filtering for matching stage, timing, and valuation tier yielded fewer than the three minimum datapoints required for statistical reliability.

Given the inapplicability of peer-median triangulation, alternative valuation methods would be necessary to establish a defensible range. Revenue or EBITDA multiples, if disclosed, could anchor an analysis against the private peer set, though the heterogeneity of business models within autonomous systems (cargo delivery, urban air mobility, last-mile logistics) limits direct comparability. Discounted cash flow analysis, if cash flow projections are available, would provide an independent cross-check but depends heavily on assumptions about market adoption and competitive positioning.

Without sufficient quantitative anchors from comparable transactions or earnings multiples, this valuation rests on material uncertainty. Key variables include Terra Drone's revenue trajectory relative to private peers, unit economics by application segment, and path to profitability. A credible range would require either expanded comps analysis across geographies or deeper diligence into the company's financial and operational metrics.
